subject.title: Feature Request: Configurable Session Lane Concurrency + Auto-Yield

question: Should OpenClaw add core session-lane concurrency and auto-yield config now, and what ordering, cancellation, and transcript-safety contract should those knobs enforce?
rationale: Source proves the requested capability is missing, but changing same-session scheduling and public config crosses session-state, transcript, cancellation, and tool-side-effect policy that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design scheduler contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define the concurrency, auto-yield, ordering, cancellation, and transcript-safety contract, while reviewing the warning-threshold PR separately.

options.title: Ship diagnostics only for now
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86676 as the near-term logging-noise fix and explicitly defer session concurrency and auto-yield.

options.title: Reject new core knobs
options.body: Close the direction in favor of existing queue steer, queue interrupt, subagent delegation, and explicit sessions_yield behavior.

recommendation.title: Design scheduler contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define the concurrency, auto-yield, ordering, cancellation, and transcript-safety contract, while reviewing the warning-threshold PR separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the command queue, embedded run lane admission, gateway lane concurrency, and config surfaces where history shows the strongest ownership signal.
